name: knock_over_with_object
doc: Knock over a target object using another specified object.
effect: The target object is knocked over by the specified object.
code:
def run(arm, object, target, **_):
    # Get the positions of the object to use for knocking and the target object
    object_pos = arm.pos(object)
    target_pos = arm.pos(target)
    grasp_z = arm.top(object) - 0.02
    hover = arm.top(object) + 0.10

    # Open the gripper, move to the object, and pick it up
    arm.open()
    arm.move_to([object_pos[0], object_pos[1], hover])
    arm.move_to([object_pos[0], object_pos[1], grasp_z])
    arm.grasp(object)
    arm.move_to([object_pos[0], object_pos[1], hover])

    # Move the object to a hover position near the target object
    arm.move_to([target_pos[0], target_pos[1], hover])

    # Position the object near the top of the target and tilt to knock over
    arm.move_to([target_pos[0], target_pos[1], arm.top(target) + 0.02])
    arm.move_to([target_pos[0], target_pos[1] + 0.05, arm.top(target)], tilt_deg=45)

    # Release the object
    arm.release()
    arm.move_to([target_pos[0], target_pos[1] + 0.05, hover])

    # Return home
    arm.home()


def check(before, after, target, **_):
    # Check if the target has tipped over
    return after["objects"][target]["tilt_deg"] == 90, f"{target} did not tip over"
